body.target_estimand: \(\tau_{[L,U]}(z^{[L,U]})=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\{Y_i^{[L,U]}(1)-[Y_i^{[L,U]}(2)+Y_i^{[L,U]}(3)]/2\}\) for a fixed complete schedule in \([L,U]^{3n}\), with the binary target \(\tau(z)\) obtained at \([L,U]=[0,1]\).
body.estimand_functional:
For fixed finite \(L<U\), with \(W=U-L\),
\[
\rho_{n,[L,U]}^{\mathrm{all}}
=W^2\{n^{-1}-C_3n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3})\},
\qquad C_3=-a_1',
\]
and, uniformly on compact sets of \(\zeta_n=n^{1/6}(q_n-q^\star)\),
\[
\rho_{n,[L,U]}^{\mathrm{iid}}(q_n)
=W^2\left[n^{-1}+n^{-4/3}\{\mathsf P(\zeta_n)-C_3\}
+o(n^{-4/3})\right].
\]

sampling_model.design: The unrestricted benchmark ranges over every law on \(\mathcal A^n\) chosen independently of the fixed complete schedule; no coordinate independence or arm positivity is imposed. The attaining comparator is iid \(q^\star\), and the allocation frontier ranges over iid triangular arrays \(q_n\).
sampling_model.units: There are \(n\) labelled units with a fixed complete schedule in \([L,U]^{3n}\), where \(-\infty<L<U<\infty\) is common to all arms and units and fixed with respect to \(n\). Binary schedules are the normalized endpoint subclass; no superpopulation sampling is invoked.
sampling_model.treatment: Each unit receives exactly one of three labelled arms and reveals only \(Y_i^{[L,U]}(A_i)\). The target is the fixed finite-population contrast with weights \((1,-1/2,-1/2)\).
sampling_model.overlap: No positivity restriction is imposed on unrestricted competing designs. Each iid frontier array is eventually interior because it converges to \(q^\star=(1/2,1/4,1/4)\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There are no estimated nuisance regressions. The bounded upper rule independently Bernoulliizes normalized observed outcomes and then analytically averages that randomization, so the reported Rao--Blackwellized estimator is a deterministic function of the realized assignment and bounded outcomes.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 2.1--2.2 identify the two-arm binary reduced experiment and Theorem 2.3 transfers its unrestricted minimax value exactly to a common bounded interval.
For two bounded-outcome arms, iid half assignment and a nonlinear endpoint-derived estimator attain the unrestricted minimax value characterized by a finite convex program.
Under the paper's permutation-invariant uncertainty class and linear-estimation formulation, complete randomization and a Neyman allocation solve the stated minimax problem.
For general multi-treatment finite-population contrasts and assignment mechanisms, the paper gives exact variance identities for linear unbiased estimators.
For multi-arm complete randomization with fixed limiting allocation proportions, regression-adjusted estimators admit regular design-based asymptotic comparisons.
Second-order asymptotic minimax behavior can be characterized by square completion and a problem-specific differential operator.
Restricted normal-mean minimax risk has a boundary-layer analysis based on least-favorable distributions.
Under design unbiasedness for bounded finite-population total estimation, pairwise-independent sampling and midpoint-differenced Horvitz--Thompson estimation attain the sharp minimax criterion.

body.tldr: For the fixed three-arm contrast \(1,-1/2,-1/2\) and any common finite outcome interval \[L,U\], an exact endpoint-transfer theorem makes the unrestricted and iid bounded minimax values \(U-L\)^2 times their binary values. The eight-type orbit game remains a literal reduction only for binary endpoint schedules. The new proved kernel identifies the half-wedge Airy constant \(C_3=-a_1^{\prime}\), establishes matching global minimax-value bounds through schedule-uniform estimators and all-design priors, and gives the sharp \(n^{-1/6}\) iid allocation frontier. A stronger fiberwise uniform liminf/recovery comparison across transverse strata remains open.

project_justification.gap: The two-arm sources and accepted binary multi-arm parent do not determine the three-arm half-wedge constant, derive its allocation frontier, or prove exact bounded endpoint transfer; a stronger transverse fiberwise experiment comparison also remains open.
project_justification.niche: For the labelled active-versus-pooled-comparators contrast, zero-sum normalization permits exact bounded endpoint transfer, while the binary endpoint adversary has genuinely three-arm half-wedge geometry and sharp global value bounds despite an unresolved stronger fiberwise comparison at eta=0.
project_justification.fill: The project proves finite-n endpoint equality, the exact half-wedge Airy constant, matching schedule-uniform and all-design global value bounds, and the necessary-and-sufficient n^(-1/6) allocation frontier. It does not claim the open fiberwise liminf/recovery theorem.

body.related_work: Sudijono, Dobriban, and Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026, Theorems 2.1--2.2) identify the balanced two-arm binary reduced experiment, and their Theorem 2.3 proves the two-arm bounded endpoint transfer that motivates the design-preserving three-arm proof here. Their Theorem 3.1 and Appendix C inform the one-dimensional Airy correction, but do not determine the labelled three-arm half-wedge constant or singular transverse bridge. The accepted repository parent \(\texttt{exp\_multiarm\_secondorder\_minimax\_frontier}\) supplies the lossless labelled eight-type reduction for binary schedules only. Hull (2026, Theorem 1 and proof A.4) informs two-arm endpoint-game and posterior-mean constructions. Mukerjee, Dasgupta, and Rubin (2018, Sections 2--3 and Theorem 1) supply general arm-labelled contrasts and unequal replication with linear unbiased estimation. Bai (2023, Theorems 3.1--3.3) informs the first-order allocation square completion; Zhao and Ding (2023) and Li and Ding (2017) provide regular multi-arm finite-population asymptotics. Levit (1981) and Bickel (1981) inform the spectral route, while Aronow and Lopatto (2026, Theorems 1--3) impose design unbiasedness, which is not imposed here.
body.interpretation: Changing the measurement scale from binary endpoints to a common interval of width \(W\) multiplies every squared-error benchmark and allocation penalty by \(W^2\), but it does not change \(q^\star\), the \(n^{-1/6}\) allocation tolerance, or the dimensionless constant \(C_3\). The continuous bounded experiment is handled by Rao--Blackwellized endpoint randomization, not by pretending each bounded response is one of eight binary types.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The bounded transfer is an exact equality of minimax values, not a literal finite-orbit representation of each continuous schedule. The proved singular statement is only a global minimax-value sandwich: the dual prior concentrates at eta=0 and does not furnish fiberwise recovery uniformly across a transverse eta-band. The stronger liminf/recovery comparison remains open.
body.honest_scope: The lossless eight-type orbit reduction is inherited and literal only for binary endpoint schedules. The endpoint theorem proves exact bounded minimax-value identities and transports estimators and priors. The singular theorem proves only matching global worst-case/Bayes value inequalities; it does not prove a uniform liminf or recovery comparison over an eta-band, a transverse-stratum comparison, cellwise Le Cam equivalence, a continuous-schedule eight-type likelihood, uniqueness of the unrestricted design, equality with fixed-count complete randomization, or exact finite-n saddle attainment. The stronger fiberwise comparison remains open.
